name: BP p.l.c.
blurb: BP is one of the world's largest integrated energy companies, headquartered in London, with operations spanning upstream oil and gas, midstream pipelines, refining, petrochemicals, and a growing low-carbon energy business. It reports earnings on a replacement-cost (RC) basis — stripping inventory holding gains — which gives a cleaner read of operational performance than GAAP. BP trades on the NYSE as an American Depositary Share (ADS).
recent: BP's Q1 2026 underlying replacement-cost profit surged to $3.2 billion ($3.8 billion on a total RC basis), more than doubling year-over-year and beating analyst expectations of $2.63 billion by 22%. The customers-and-products (refining and trading) segment delivered an extraordinary swing of $2.5 billion versus the prior year, driven by refining margin expansion and exceptional oil-trading results in a highly volatile crude market. BP ADS EPS of $1.24 beat the Zacks consensus of $0.91 by 36%. The Hormuz disruption boosted both upstream realizations and physical oil trading profits simultaneously — a rare confluence that analysts expect to moderate in Q2 as the market normalizes.
